questions.formal_statement: Challenge5: rigorously calculate improved upper bounds for SAT/UNSAT phase transitions in random k-SAT; focus on k=4 and5 within this visit.
questions.relation_to_book: The book explicitly requests certified bounds via interval arithmetic or other rigorous numerical methods. k=4,5 improvements would address part of that challenge, not solve all five challenges or determine exact thresholds.
questions.solved_means: For k=4 and k=5, rational a_k below 10.23 and 21.33 with complete proofs that random k-SAT (independent clauses, distinct uniformly chosen variables, independent fair signs) with floor(a_k n) clauses is unsatisfiable with probability tending to one.

identified_counterpart.zh_quote: 面临的挑战 5 如果以上提到的技巧(或者其他技巧)可以有效地用于种群动力学模拟，那么这必将极大程度增进对 K-SAT 问题的满足/不满足相变点和其他相变点的上下限的严格计算。这将会成为理论计算机科学的一个非常重要的成果。
identified_counterpart.en: Challenge 5. If the techniques mentioned above (or other techniques) could be applied effectively to population-dynamics simulations, this would greatly advance the rigorous computation of the upper and lower bounds (上下限) on the satisfiable/unsatisfiable (SAT/UNSAT) transition point and on other transition points of the K-SAT problem. This would be a very important achievement for theoretical computer science. [Context on the same page, which says what 'the techniques mentioned above' are: 'According to Guerra's work, the exact solution of the 1RSB integral equations would give a rigorous variational bound (printed 上下限, literally "upper and lower bound") on the SAT/UNSAT transition point [9]. Research groups around the world have independently applied population dynamics, including one of us [21,22]. Many numerical simulation schemes in analysis and mathematical physics can give rigorous upper and lower bounds by means of certain techniques (such as interval arithmetic, 区间代数法). The most famous example is the existence of a fixed point of the Feigenbaum operator in the theory of dynamical systems, first proved by O. Lanford; a separate review can be found in [13].' Just before this (PDF pp. 458–459, book pp. 425–426), the article says that statistical-physics predictions for CSPs depend on numerically solving very complex integral equations, the 1RSB cavity-field equations, defined either for a single large instance or for an ensemble. Their solutions are probability distributions. Population dynamics, the only known numerical scheme, needs an initial distribution, and different initial distributions can lead to different fixed points.]

identified_counterpart.formal_statement:
LITERAL BOOK STATEMENT (Challenge 5, PDF p. 459). The challenge is conditional and reads as a research program. If interval-arithmetic-type techniques 'or other techniques' could be applied effectively to population-dynamics simulations of the 1RSB cavity equations, this would greatly advance the rigorous computation of 上下限 (upper and lower bounds) on the SAT/UNSAT transition point and on other transition points of random K-SAT. The book fixes no K and gives no numerical targets.

NARROWED QUESTION (owner focus). Model: fix k ∈ {4, 5} (the article's K). For n ≥ k and α > 0, let Φ = Φ_k(n, α) be a random k-CNF on n Boolean variables (Ising spins σ_i ∈ {−1, +1}) with m = ⌊αn⌋ clauses. Each clause a independently picks a set ∂a of k distinct variables uniformly at random and a forbidden pattern (J_{ai})_{i∈∂a} ∈ {−1, +1}^k uniformly at random. Clause a is violated iff σ_i = J_{ai} for all i ∈ ∂a. [ASSUMPTION: the article only says that each clause's K variables are chosen at random among the N and that each clause removes one of the 2^K joint values. The uniform forbidden pattern and the exact ensemble (with or without replacement; ⌊αn⌋ or Poisson(αn) clauses) are standard choices I supplied.] Energy: H_Φ(σ) = number of clauses violated by σ, as in the article.

Definition [ASSUMPTION: phrased so that it does not presuppose a limiting threshold for k = 4, 5]: a real u is a rigorous upper bound for the SAT/UNSAT transition of random k-SAT if, for every α > u, lim_{n→∞} P(Φ_k(n, α) is satisfiable) = 0.

Task: for each k ∈ {4, 5}, give an explicit constant u_k and a rigorous proof that u_k is a rigorous upper bound in this sense, with u_k < U_k*. The proof may be analytic, or computer-assisted with every numerical step certified (for example by interval arithmetic). U_k* is the best rigorous upper bound established in the literature before the attempt. [ASSUMPTION: the article gives no baseline values; U_k* must come from the literature check.] No valid u_k can lie below the true threshold. The cavity-method estimates of [15] (the article's 'most precise estimates so far' of the transition point, citing [15,16]) are therefore the conjectured limit of improvement. [ASSUMPTION]

ROUTE NAMED BY THE ARTICLE (context, not a requirement, since the book allows '或者其他技巧'). The article states three things. (1) By Guerra's work, the exact solution of the 1RSB integral equations gives 'a rigorous variational 上下限' on the SAT/UNSAT point [9]. (2) Those solutions are probability distributions, currently obtainable only by population dynamics, which needs an initial distribution and may reach different fixed points. (3) Interval-arithmetic-type techniques give rigorous bounds in other numerical problems (Lanford's Feigenbaum fixed point; review [13]). The article does not say which side of the transition the Guerra bound controls.

[ASSUMPTION, to be verified against [9] and later literature] The Guerra/Franz–Leone interpolation bound is one-sided. For every β > 0, every Parisi parameter m ∈ (0, 1] and every trial 1RSB order parameter (a law on laws of cavity fields): limsup_n (1/n) E log Σ_σ exp(−β H_Φ(σ)) ≤ P_1RSB(α, β, m, trial). Since log Z ≥ −β min_σ H_Φ(σ), this gives liminf_n (1/n) E min_σ H_Φ(σ) ≥ −P_1RSB/β. If this explicit quantity is certified > 0 at density α, then by concentration of min_σ H_Φ the formula Φ is unsatisfiable w.h.p., so α is a rigorous upper bound. On this reading: (a) the route gives only upper bounds on the SAT/UNSAT density, via lower bounds on the ground-state energy; (b) the bound holds for any explicit trial, and solving the 1RSB equations exactly only makes it as tight as possible. A certificate then needs rigorous evaluation of the functional at one explicit trial (for example a finitely supported, population-dynamics-derived one), with controlled truncation of Poisson-degree sums. It does not need certified convergence of population dynamics. (c) Whether [9] as published covers odd K (needed for k = 5) must be checked.

EXCLUDED BY THE NARROWING (but present in the literal challenge): rigorous lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point; bounds on 'other transition points' (e.g., the solution-space transitions of Fig. 1, ref. [14]); k other than 4 and 5; exact thresholds; a general rigorous population-dynamics methodology.
identified_counterpart.solved_means: For the narrowed question, a full solution needs, for each of k = 4 and k = 5, an explicit constant u_k with a complete, checkable rigorous proof that random k-SAT with clause density α > u_k is unsatisfiable with probability tending to 1. The proof may be analytic, or computer-assisted with every numerical step certified (e.g., interval arithmetic with controlled rounding, plus explicit truncation and tail bounds for Poisson-degree sums and trial-measure expectations). u_k must be strictly below the best rigorous upper bound available before the attempt. The article supplies no baseline, so the literature stage should find both the 2009-era bound and the current best. Improving only one of k = 4, 5 is partial success. Following the book's route (certified evaluation of the Guerra/Franz–Leone 1RSB variational bound at an explicit, e.g. population-dynamics-derived, trial order parameter) addresses the book's methodological challenge directly. An improvement by other rigorous means settles the narrowed numerical question but bears only partly on the book's program. Not required: matching lower bounds, exact thresholds, bounds on clustering/condensation or other transitions, or other k. The full literal Challenge 5 would further need a general rigorous (validated-numerics) treatment of population dynamics, giving rigorous upper and lower bounds on the SAT/UNSAT point and other transition points.

literature.summary: For k=4,5, q1 is open in this check as of 2026-10-15: no certified improvement beyond the classical benchmarks reported by [Achlioptas–Peres (2004)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0305009v2) was located. [Lelarge–Oulamara (2018)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1708.02457) provides a suitable variational framework, including odd SAT arity, but neither it nor the recent related claims supplies the missing numerical pair.

sources.citation: Alava, Aurell and 周海军, 《用统计物理学方法处理约束满足问题面临的五个挑战》, 《10000个科学难题·物理学卷》, pp. 422–427.
sources.finding: Direct PDF opening failed, although indexed Chinese excerpts corroborated Challenge 5 and identified reference [9] as Franz–Leone. The chapter proposes a broader research program without fixed k or numerical targets. Exact-title citation searches identified no direct citing resolution; this search silence is not evidence of openness.

sources.citation: Achlioptas and Peres, [The threshold for random k-SAT is 2^k log 2 − O(k)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0305009v2), JAMS 17, 947–973.
sources.finding: The introduction reports upper bounds 10.23 for k=4 and 21.33 for k=5, crediting earlier upper-bound papers. Its new results are lower bounds, including 7.91 and 18.79. The independent uniform-clause model matches the requested ensemble.

sources.citation: Kirousis, Kranakis, Krizanc and Stamatiou, [Approximating the unsatisfiability threshold of random formulas](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/%28SICI%291098-2418%28199805%2912%3A3%3C253%3A%3AAID-RSA3%3E3.0.CO%3B2-U), Random Structures & Algorithms 12, 253–269.
sources.finding: Publisher abstract and a full-text transcription were opened. The model explicitly uses distinct variables within clauses, independent uniform signs, and clauses sampled independently with replacement. Theorem 2 gives a rigorous upper bound R_k defined by (1−2^(−k))^R_k [2−exp(−k R_k/(2^k−1))]=1. Thus the familiar two-decimal table entries are not exact novelty baselines.

Table 8.1 confirms the 2009-era reported upper bounds 10.23 and 21.33. The chapter attributes the general-k sharpening independently to Dubois–Boufkhad and Kirousis et al. Its introductory ensemble samples clauses without replacement; the original Kirousis theorem directly covers the requested with-replacement ensemble.

sources.citation: Friedrich, Krohmer, Rothenberger, Sauerwald and Sutton, [Bounds on the Satisfiability Threshold for Power Law Distributed Random SAT](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol087-esa2017/LIPIcs.ESA.2017.37/LIPIcs.ESA.2017.37.pdf), ESA 2017, Article 37.
sources.finding: Theorem 1.2 generalizes single-flip counting to nonuniform variable distributions. Its uniform specialization reproduces the classical inequality; Table 1 reports 10.23 and 21.33 and identifies the uniform k≥4 entries as the best numerical upper bounds known to its authors. Smaller power-law entries concern different ensembles.

sources.citation: Franz and Leone, [Replica bounds for optimization problems and diluted spin systems](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/0208280), Journal of Statistical Physics 111, 535–564.
sources.finding: The bound is one-sided: lower bounds on physical free energy and ground-state energy yield upper bounds on SAT density. The accessible 2002 full-text version explicitly restricts its rigorous argument to even arity; odd arity invokes additional overlap assumptions. The 2003 publisher abstract was also opened, but its subscription full text was unavailable. This reference alone therefore supplies no checked unconditional k=5 bridge.

sources.citation: Panchenko and Talagrand, [Bounds for diluted mean-fields spin glass models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405357), Probability Theory and Related Fields 130, 319–336.
sources.finding: Gives replica variational upper bounds on normalized expected log partition functions, including hierarchical trial distributions. The paper fixes an even integer p≥2 throughout. It cannot simply be cited as an unrestricted odd-k theorem.

sources.citation: Achlioptas and Menchaca-Mendez, [Unsatisfiability Bounds for Random CSPs from an Energetic Interpolation Method](https://cgi.di.uoa.gr/~optas/papers/Energetic.pdf), ICALP 2012, pp. 1–12.
sources.finding: Proves a computable energetic lower bound on minimum violated constraints using a single warning probability. The SAT argument applies to general k, including odd k, through convexity on nonnegative arguments. Section 7 reduces evaluation to nonnegative Poisson sums that can be truncated rigorously. Its explicit application concerns mixed 2/3-SAT; it does not supply improved uniform k=4,5 constants.

angles.angle: During the first two hours, audit the general-k energetic comparison against Lelarge–Oulamara Theorem 3, explicitly specializing nonnegative SAT factors for k=4 and odd k=5. Use exact small-instance checks to test any newly proposed replacement inequality.
angles.deliverable: A written admissibility and comparison lemma with controlled finite-temperature/finite-y limits, or an exact counterexample locating a failed step. Do not infer the lemma from numerical negativity or from the k=3 preprint's claimed formalization.

angles.angle: Search finite warning trials with rational support and weights, starting at the comfortable candidate densities 249/25=9.96 and 1057/50=21.14. Certify expectations using rational enclosures for logarithms and exponentials, rigorously signed truncation, and explicit Poisson tails.
angles.deliverable: Explicit trial data and an independently replayable Python rational/interval checker proving a negative functional margin. If the analytic comparison remains unproved, report only that certified inequality conditional on the stated comparison.

angles.angle: Complete the finite-model implications after a positive linear expected-energy bound: couple Poisson and fixed clause counts, resample clauses with repeated variables, then apply bounded-difference concentration and monotonicity.
angles.deliverable: Explicit loss estimates, including E|Poisson(αn)−floor(αn)|≤sqrt(αn)+1 and an O(1) expected repeated-variable replacement cost for fixed k, followed by the requested high-probability theorem if all preceding steps succeed.

angles.angle: If the proposed energetic extension fails, evaluate the published finite-temperature variational bound directly at bounded-field finite trials instead of continuing with the invalid extension.
angles.deliverable: A certified trial inequality within the published theorem's hypotheses, or a documented finite-search obstruction. Any restricted result remains partial progress on Challenge 5.

acceptance.solved: For k=4 and k=5, rational a_k below 10.23 and 21.33 with complete proofs that random k-SAT (independent clauses, distinct uniformly chosen variables, independent fair signs) with floor(a_k n) clauses is unsatisfiable with probability tending to one.
acceptance.refuted: a verified counterexample or negative answer to the stated question itself
acceptance.partial: An exactly scoped verified result: a fully proved bound for one k, or a certified trial-functional inequality explicitly conditional on stated unproved analytic bridges.

owner_selection.title_zh: 用统计物理学方法处理约束满足问题面临的五个挑战
owner_selection.question: Challenge5: rigorously calculate improved upper bounds for SAT/UNSAT phase transitions in random k-SAT; focus on k=4 and5 within this visit.
owner_selection.relation_to_book: The book explicitly requests certified bounds via interval arithmetic or other rigorous numerical methods. k=4,5 improvements would address part of that challenge, not solve all five challenges or determine exact thresholds.
owner_selection.baseline: Opened Achlioptas-Peres table: upper bounds10.23(k=4),21.33(k=5),87.88(k=7). Recheck current literature. Vorobyev2610.10599 claims4.268 for k=3 only; it is an unrefereed method lead.
owner_selection.bounded_target: Aim for certified rational a4<10.23 and a5<21.33 proving P[random distinct-variable k-SAT with floor(ak*n) clauses is satisfiable]->0. Probes suggest9.94 and21.125 but are not certificates. Improvements remain partial book-level progress.
owner_selection.angle: Establish the general-k energetic interpolation inequality and its model transfer; then certify a rational multi-warning trial with rigorous truncation/error bounds and an independent checker, starting with k=4,5. Use k=3 reproduction and known satisfiable densities as controls.
owner_selection.risk: The analytic bridge, Poisson/fixed-count and repeated/distinct-variable transfer, and series/error signs are load-bearing. A negative functional alone is only conditional evidence. No Lean validation of the cited preprint has been performed; do not claim a kernel-checked theorem. Success confidence is speculative.
review_requirements: Use three claim levels: floating-point negativity is evidence only; exact or interval negativity with rigorously signed truncation is a certified inequality only; a threshold theorem requires every analytic bridge to be written and accepted.

Threshold target: for each k in {4,5}, exhibit rational a_k below 10.23 and 21.33 respectively and prove P[F_k(n, floor(a_k n)) is satisfiable]->0 with independent clauses, uniformly chosen distinct variables within each clause, and independent fair signs.

Prove the general-k interpolation inequality for each selected k, explicitly checking odd k=5 hypotheses; finite-y or y-limit control; expectation-to-high-probability concentration; and Poisson/fixed-count plus repeated/distinct-variable transfers with explicit losses. Numerical replay cannot discharge these obligations. Vorobyev k=3 work is only a method lead.
Before using improves, recover the original source and random model behind the 10.23 and 21.33 baselines. Check Achlioptas-Menchaca-Mendez 2012 and its citing works for existing k>=4 numbers.
Tripwire: a value at or below cavity estimates 9.931 (k=4) or 21.117 (k=5) is a probable bug. Certify comfortable margins first (around k=4 at 9.96; k=5 at or above 21.14), not k=5 at 21.125.
Decide by about two attack hours whether the interpolation inequality holds; build certificate tools in parallel. Success confidence is speculative; 9.94 and 21.125 are search targets only.

Without all analytic bridges, report only a certified negative trial-functional value conditional on the stated inequality. Even with them, this is partial progress on Challenge 5: no lower bounds, no exact thresholds, and no solution of the broader program.

owner_selection.partial_means: An exactly scoped verified result: a fully proved bound for one k, or a certified trial-functional inequality explicitly conditional on stated unproved analytic bridges.
shared_scope_rules: No automatic revisit, refill, extra problem, paid-API fallback, model/config change, scheduler, commit, push, or external contact.
A special case, finite search range, or improved bound is partial progress, not resolution of a broader book question.
Sampling is not independent exhaustive verification. Numerical negativity is not a theorem without its analytic bridge. Solver UNKNOWN is not UNSAT.
Openness and novelty are dated search verdicts. Preprints and openai/math are claims until independently established.
shared_review_overrides: This manifest and parent restrictions override stronger promises, confidence labels, and schedules in the screening catalogs.
The 14,400-second attack is part of each 21,600-second visit, not an extra allowance. Early termination and inconclusive outcomes are valid; no refill is implied.
Reserve new best, improved, or novel wording for the visit literature and novelty assessments; reproduction and restricted results keep their exact scope.

The replay sandbox forbids executing binaries created inside the attack directory. Every claims.json verify/check/control command must run with python3 or preinstalled system tools; preserve compiled-production logs as evidence instead.
